question.prompt: Through a point \(P\) inside triangle \(ABC\) a line is drawn parallel to the base \(\overline{AB},\) dividing the triangle into two equal areas. If the altitude to \(\overline{AB}\) has length \(1,\) then the distance from \(P\) to \(\overline{AB}\) is:

solutions.explanation:
Let the line through \(P\) meet \(AC\) and \(BC\) at \(M\) and \(N\), respectively. Since \(MN\parallel AB\), corresponding angles are equal, so \(\triangle CMN\) is similar to \(\triangle CAB\).

Let \(d\) be the perpendicular distance from \(P\) to \(AB\). Because \(P\) is inside the triangle, \(0<d<1\). The altitude from \(C\) to \(MN\) is \(1-d\), while the original altitude is 1. Thus the similarity ratio is \(1-d\).

Areas of similar triangles have the square of their length ratio. The upper triangle has half the original area, so
\[
(1-d)^2=\frac12.
\]
Since \(1-d>0\), we take the positive square root:
\[
1-d=\frac1{\sqrt2},
\qquad
 d=1-\frac{\sqrt2}{2}
=\frac{2-\sqrt2}{2}.
\]
The required distance is \(\boxed{\dfrac{2-\sqrt2}{2}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Use the area ratio of similar triangles
